title: Harbor Aviation — outbound pilot sketch & objection bank
content:
Context / why this target: Harbor Aviation is a mid-size regional carrier (operations in NA + some EU routes) exploring modernizing their on-board crew-assist and maintenance triage workflows with LLMs. From analyst notes and investor deck snippets: high interest in predictive maintenance, SOP summarization for crews, and passenger-facing chat for schedule disruptions. They are conservative on safety and compliance — expect long procurement cycles but a high ACV once satisfied.

Primary contacts to hunt down (notes from LinkedIn + event list):
- Chief Digital Officer (CDO) — likely decision sponsor for data/ops; focus on fleet-level ops improvements.
- Head of Engineering (infrastructure) — cares about VPC/on-prem options, KMS, latency to edge.
- Director of Safety & Compliance — gatekeeper for anything touching flight ops / SOPs.
- Head of Customer Experience — end-user champion for passenger chat features.

Quick account research:
- Fleet: regional jets, mostly Boeing/Embraer (short-to-medium haul). Onboard compute varies by partner vendor; many connected via ground-based comms windows.
- Existing vendor stack: they have a mix of legacy maintenance software + a SaaS CRM for customer ops. Some internal ML work but limited infra.
- Compliance: EU routes mean GDPR; aviation-specific regs mean any cockpit/SOP assistant must pass rigorous validation and change-control.

Hypothesis for fit (how Redwood helps):
- Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) to keep PII and safety-related prompts within their network — key ask from Safety & Compliance.
- Low-latency inference and on-edge batching for crew-assist use cases (short prompts, constrained context) vs. bulk post-flight summarization for maintenance (batch inference, embeddings + similarity search).
- Rollout strategy: start with non-safety-critical passenger chat (customer experience) to get buy-in and anonymized prompts, then pilot maintenance triage as proof of cost savings, finally SOP summarization with compliance-validated evaluation sets.

Pilot proposal (sketch):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): discovery + prompt cataloging. Remote workshops with ops + safety to capture 50 canonical prompts across crew, maintenance, CX. Baseline metrics for latency, precision, false-alarm rates.
- Phase 1 (6–8 weeks): CX pilot — deploy hosted Redwood API integrated into web/mobile chat for a subset of flights. Measure deflection, response latency, CSAT.
- Phase 2 (8–12 weeks): Maintenance triage — internal tool that takes post-flight logs, generates prioritized tickets with suggested triage steps. Run in shadow mode alongside existing workflows.
- Optional Phase 3: On-prem/private deployment for SOP assistant — full audit trail, model pinning, and evaluation harness to validate outputs against certified SOPs.

Value props & KPIs to lead with:
- Time-to-first-value: get CX pilot live in 6–8 weeks without long infra procurement.
- Latency: median response <300ms for crew-assist UI target (explain tradeoffs with batching).
- Cost: projected token-cost reduction vs naive hosted LLM via Redwood Optimize + caching suggestions.
- Safety: audit logs, model version pinning, and evals (precision / hallucination rate on pre-defined prompt set).

Outbound messaging (subject + 3 variants):
- Subject A: "Quick idea to cut crew cognitive load during turnarounds"
  - 1-line opener: "Maya from Redwood — we help airlines reduce crew admin and speed triage by combining a private inference runtime with safety-first evals. Can I share a 6-week pilot plan?"
- Subject B: "Pilot: private LLM to assist maintenance triage (no flight-data leaves your VPC)"
  - Opener: "Not a vendor pitch — a lightweight pilot plan that keeps all logs inside your network. Interested in a 15-min scoping call?"
- Subject C: "CX automation idea for disrupted flights — reduce calls during delays"
  - Opener: "We reduced call volume by 22% for a regional carrier in a short pilot; happy to share how we might do the same for Harbor Aviation."

Cold sequence (4 touches, rough):
- Day 0: Short email to CDO with Subject A, link to 1-pager + ask for 15-min intro.
- Day 3: LinkedIn message to Head of CX referencing brief stat and a testimonial.
- Day 7: Follow-up email with concrete pilot timeline and light NDA offer.
- Day 14: Internal champion outreach (if connected) or final quick note offering calendar times.

Anticipated objections & rebuttals (bank):
- Objection: "Safety/regulatory risk — we can't use LLMs in ops."
  - Rebuttal: "Start outside safety-critical flows (CX/maintenance triage shadow mode). For SOP assistant, propose a phased validation plan + audit logs + model pinning; show eval pass rates and a change-control process."
- Objection: "We can't send flight logs to a vendor (data residency)."
  - Rebuttal: "Redwood Private supports VPC + on-prem; we can demo a local deployment with KMS integration and no data egress. Also offer a short architecture diagram and drop-in demo environment for infra team to vet."
- Objection: "Latency/air-gapped connectivity on aircraft is a blocker."
  - Rebuttal: "For in-flight crew-assist we suggest a mixed strategy: pre-loaded prompts + edge inference for critical flows or temporary offline mode; for ground operations, ground-based low-latency endpoints. We'll profile their telemetry to recommend kernels/batching settings."
- Objection: "Costs are unclear / too expensive."
  - Rebuttal: "Show Redwood Optimize analysis — quantify token-level savings, caching, and estimated per-ticket cost; propose a fixed-cost pilot so they can evaluate ROI with predictable price."

Technical / infra notes to prep for technical scoping:
- Need to confirm: network topology (do they allow VPC peering?), preferred KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault), and existing on-prem hardware if they want air-gapped.
- Sequence length expectations for crew-assist (likely short, <512 tokens). Maintenance logs may be large — plan for chunking + embeddings.
- Logging & audit needs for Safety: immutable logs, model version + prompt capture, and RBAC for access to logs.
- Integration points: ticketing system (ServiceNow/Jira), mobile/web SDKs, and flight ops dashboards.

Pricing sketch to discuss (internal note):
- Offer a 3-month pilot at $X (placeholder) covering infra overhead + engineering support (we'll convert to actual numbers before sending). Alternatively propose cost-sharing where we bill only for engineering hours and they cover infra.

Call prep checklist (for first scoping call):
- 10-min intros: roles and success metrics.
- 15-min discovery: current pain points for CX / maintenance / ops.
- 10-min technical: infra constraints (KMS, VPC, air-gap), telemetry availability.
- Ask for next materials: sample sanitized prompts / example maintenance logs, contact for safety/compliance.

Open questions (to answer before pilot proposal):
- Do they have a central data lake of post-flight logs? (yes/no)
- Can they sign a mutual NDA quickly?
- Who owns vendor integrations for cockpit tools vs. ground ops?
- Any existing internal ML models we should co-locate with?

Next steps (my to-dos):
- Draft one-pager tailored to Harbor Aviation (deadline: 2024-02-14). Ethan to add high-level architecture diagram.
- Ask Solutions Eng to prepare a short demo showing VPC + KMS flow (target: 2024-02-16).
- Pull a short case study of regional carrier CX pilot (Sofia to find contact & permission).
- Create evaluation prompt set template for Safety to review (I will draft prompts).

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Keep the language safety-first; any outbound content should preempt "we're not ready" by offering shadow-mode and on-prem path.
- Might be able to accelerate via partner channel with an avionics integrator they already use — check procurement notes.
- Put the initial pilot under a low-cost retainer to get buy-in without complex procurement.

End of scratchpad: still rough, will iterate after scoping call.
